title: Solomon
lead: David's son by Bathsheba and the third king of Israel (about 970–931 BC), famous for his wisdom, wealth and the Temple he built in Jerusalem, and remembered also for the many wives and foreign gods that split his kingdom after him.

sections.b: Solomon is born to David and Bathsheba after the death of their first child, and the prophet Nathan names him Jedidiah, "loved by the LORD" (2 Samuel 12:24–25). He comes to the throne through a palace struggle with his older brother Adonijah (1 Kings 1–2), asks God for wisdom (1 Kings 3), builds the Temple and his palace (1 Kings 6–8), and grows rich from trade (1 Kings 10). His foreign wives turn his heart, and God tears most of the kingdom from his son (1 Kings 11). Chronicles tells his reign without the struggle for the throne or the late apostasy (2 Chronicles 1–9). Tradition credits him with Proverbs, Ecclesiastes and the Song of Songs (Proverbs 1:1; Ecclesiastes 1:1; Song of Songs 1:1), and two psalms bear his name (Psalm 72; Psalm 127). Nehemiah holds him up as a warning (Nehemiah 13:26), and Jesus names him twice, for his splendor and his wisdom (Matthew 6:29; Matthew 12:42).
